title: Smear
description: A quiet photo essay in big lowercase lines. Scroll slowly and it holds still; scroll hard and every photo and line smears in uneven vertical bands and burns out toward white, then snaps back sharp the moment you slow down.
intent: Speed made visible as light: the award-studio scroll-sync smear on real photographs and on the type itself, glued to native scroll with no scroll-jacking, crisp at rest.

sources.name: Lusion, WebGL Scroll Sync
sources.what: Ported (MIT): the 5-tap smear gated per column band by the sin-then-hash trick, the overexposure 1 + 2s, the strength rule s *= exp(-10 dt) + min(10|dy|/vh, 5), the per-frame re-roll of the band seeds, and the padded canvas that rides with the page between frames. The resting jitter is removed so it snaps fully sharp.

sources.name: Dave Hoskins, Hash without Sine
sources.what: hash43, as used by the Lusion shader.

sources.name: Photographs
sources.what: Herb's own prints from Scorch, used with permission and re-encoded for this page.
